name: RDBMS
tagline: Early-1970s MIT relational data management system, presented at the 1974 SIGFIDET workshop.
description: RDBMS, the Relational Data Management System, was one of the first implemented relational systems, built at MIT in the early 1970s and described by James Steuert and Jay Goldman in 'The Relational Data Management System: A Perspective' at the 1974 ACM SIGFIDET workshop, the same proceedings that introduced IBM's SEQUEL. It belongs to the first wave of prototypes that turned Codd's relational model into working software, alongside System R, Ingres and Honeywell's later MRDS. Little technical detail survives outside the paper, and the system was never distributed. It is listed here for the history of the relational model, not for any practical use.
statusNote: Early-1970s MIT research system documented in a 1974 workshop paper; never distributed. Its ideas fed the relational systems that followed.

pricing.notes: Never distributed; only the paper remains.

strengths: One of the earliest working implementations of Codd's relational model
Primary source for how relational ideas were first put into practice
weaknesses: No surviving code or documentation beyond the workshop paper
Predates SQL, transactions theory and cost-based optimisation
useCases: History of databases and the relational model
Reading lists for database systems courses
notIdealFor: Any practical workload: nothing is available to run
